blocks.text: Quito: the main square and city neighbourhoods under cloudy skies

After breakfast, explore Quito on a sightseeing tour and travel to the equator. The full programme takes about 8 hours, including transfers.

Quito sits at an altitude of 2,800 m. Its historic centre grew on the site of an older settlement and retains its colonial street plan, squares, churches and richly decorated interiors. The tour introduces the Quito School, which brought together Spanish, Italian, Moorish and Flemish traditions with Indigenous art.

On a walk through the Old Town, you will see how religious architecture and administrative buildings shaped the centre of the capital. Quito takes its name from the Quitu people, who lived here before the Spanish conquest. In 1533, the city came under the rule of Sebastián de Belalcázar. In 1541, it gained the status of a Spanish city under the name San Francisco de Quito.

The Franciscans were the first religious order to establish itself in the city. Their monastery became an important centre of education and the arts. The programme includes a visit to San Francisco Church.

Plaza Grande is home to the Cathedral, the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop’s Palace and City Hall. You will also visit a Jesuit church with a carved façade and an intricately decorated interior.

The next stop is El Panecillo. The viewpoint overlooks both the old and newer parts of Quito, with a winged statue of the Virgin Mary rising above the city.

After the city tour, you will head to the equator to visit two sites.

**Mitad del Mundo.** This visitor complex commemorates the geodetic expedition of 1736. Between 1979 and 1982, a 30 m monument was erected here and a line was drawn to mark the equator. Later GPS measurements showed that the actual equator lies about 240 m farther north.

**Intiñan Museum.** The museum demonstrates experiments associated with its position on the equator and introduces the cultures of Indigenous peoples. The grounds feature totems, traditional dwellings and everyday objects. One house contains belongings of an Indigenous family that lived in the area many generations ago.

Return to the hotel after the tour.

**Accommodation:** Plaza Grande 5*, Royal Suite.  
**Meals:** Breakfast.

Quito at dusk: a rain-slick square and fountain beneath a pink sky

After breakfast, you will head to Cotopaxi National Park. The day’s programme lasts about 8 hours, including transfers. The drive from Quito to Cotopaxi takes about 2 hours. The tour reaches an altitude of 3,800 m. The overnight stop is at about 1,800 m, where temperatures are around +20 °C during the day and +10 °C at night.

On the way, you will visit a rose farm in the Cotopaxi Valley, where flowers are grown for export. You will see roses of different colours and sizes, along with how they are cut, sorted and packed. The farm is closed to visitors on weekends and public holidays.

The route then enters Cotopaxi National Park. Established in 1975, the park covers 33,393 ha across the provinces of Pichincha, Cotopaxi and Napo. It is home to the Cotopaxi, Rumiñahui and Sincholagua volcanoes, as well as Lake Limpiopungo.

Cotopaxi rises to 5,897 m. Records of its activity date back to 1534. On a clear day, the volcano is the most prominent landmark on the surrounding plain.

Lake Limpiopungo is home to a variety of birds, including 24 wetland species, 15 of which are migratory, as well as the rare white-necked ibis. The wild rabbit is the most common mammal here. The tour includes a walk along the edge of a pine forest and a visit to the lake.

After the tour, transfer to your accommodation and spend the evening at leisure.

**Accommodation:** La Cienega 4*.  
**Meals:** Breakfast.
